title: Timing, Geometry, and the Limits of Gaussianity
subtitle: Data × learning rate · Muon initialization · Graph tests · Kaplan scaling laws
intro: Three main reads connect joint schedules, initialization geometry, and moment criteria for graph statistics. Fourteen briefs cover Muon, scaling, and post-training blogs. The classic revisits Kaplan scaling laws to separate data, model, step, and parallelism budgets.

articles.paper: Data Schedules and Learning Rate Schedules Should Be Designed Together
articles.authors: Haodong Wen · Kairong Luo · Tingkai Yan · Wenguang Chen · Kaifeng Lyu
articles.title: When good data enters depends on when the learning rate decays
articles.dateNote: First posted 2026-10-21 03:42 EDT · v1; listed October 22
articles.evidence: Read §§2–3, theoretical interpretation, and experimental setup; not reproduced

blocks.text: Let γ(t) be the mid-training (MT) fraction and η(t) the learning rate. With compute and MT tokens fixed, introducing MT earlier can win under decay and lose under constant LR. [1]

blocks.label: γ allocates data; R is the cumulative learning rate available to MT-specific features

blocks.text: The explanation uses block-diagonal quadratics and additive gradient noise. Extract one MT-specific direction with curvature λ>0, initial value z₀, variance ν, and discrete-step interval h. [1]

blocks.label: One-direction form of the paper's linear SDE: bias followed by variance

blocks.text: With constant η, spending the budget fixes R(0); placing MT last maximizes every R(s), minimizing variance. Under decay, moving MT earlier also raises R(0), creating a bias–variance trade-off. [1]

rows: Full decay favors earlier mixing; constant LR favors final pure MT
Data schedule fixed within each scan
Best tested decay starts after MT entry
blocks.caption: Outcome: final MT validation loss, rather than downstream capability or a universal recipe. [1]

blocks.title: Evidence boundary
blocks.text: The SDE assumes fixed additive noise. Its power-law three-stage optimum requires further assumptions and long horizons; the decomposition alone does not establish an optimum for general LLM training. [1]

articles.paper: Third and Fourth Moment Phenomena for Monochromatic Edges and Applications to Graph-Based Two-Sample Tests
articles.authors: Siva Athreya · Bhaswar B. Bhattacharya · Yogesh Dahiya · Karambir Das · Spandan Ghoshal · Sourish Maniyar · Elizabeth Sara Roy
articles.title: When the third moment detects Gaussianity better than the fourth
articles.evidence: Read §1 main theorems, two-sample setting, and counterexample discussion

blocks.text: Graph two-sample tests count between-group edges in a pooled similarity graph. Under the Poissonized null, conditioning on locations gives independent Bernoulli(p) labels. Balanced and unbalanced proportions require different Gaussian criteria. [3]

blocks.label: Simple undirected graphs; independent Bernoulli(p) labels with fixed p∈(0,1)

rows: E[Uₙ³]→0; the fourth-moment criterion loses discrimination
E[Uₙ⁴]→3; the third moment alone is insufficient
blocks.caption: Theorem 1.1; the exceptional p values are essential. [3]

blocks.text: A star graph explains the exception: conditioning on its center leaves a two-point limit. This is a simplified derivation of the paper's star example. [3]

blocks.label: Z is the two-point limit: fourth moment 3 does not make its distribution Gaussian

blocks.title: Evidence boundary
blocks.text: For pₙ→0 the third-moment condition stays sufficient but is no longer necessary. The two-sample application uses Poissonization, rather than every fixed-size permutation null. [3]

articles.paper: Hybrid Momentum Methods for Optimizing Deep Learning Models
articles.authors: Haifeng Xu · Yijin Ren · Chenyu Zhou · Qi Deng · Dongdong Ge · Yinyu Ye
articles.title: HyMUON combines long-history averaging with a fast EMA
articles.dateNote: First October 20; v2 October 21 05:25 EDT; overlap-window addition
articles.evidence: Read v2 method and C4 setup; version diff not fully checked

blocks.text: HyM blends long-history averaging with fast momentum; HyMUON then applies NS. LLaMA-1.3B/C4 at 10k steps gives validation loss 2.777 versus 2.903. HyMUON is tuned and evaluates averaged iterates; Muon uses previously selected settings and training iterates. The v2 note concerns author order/affiliations; no substantive new result is confirmed. [4]

articles.paper: Physics-Inspired Optimizers beyond the Edge of Stability: Period-Two Orbits and Delayed Instability
articles.title: Kinetic Muon: the step map changes period-two stability
articles.dateNote: First October 19 17:40 EDT · v1; overlap-window addition
articles.evidence: Read abstract and Muon-related experimental passages

blocks.text: Kinetic maps wrap update directions, including Muon. In the reduced model, period-two linear stability requires step-length elasticity in (0,1). Many ResNet-18 gains can be reproduced by matching effective LR, so default-LR comparisons are insufficient. [5]

articles.paper: Don't Stop Long-Context Continual Pre-Training Too Early: An Empirical Scaling Law
articles.authors: Ziqing Qiao · Xiaoyue Xu · Sikui Zhang · Yinuo Xu · Bingxiang He · Chaojun Xiao · Xu Han
articles.title: Long-context continuation separates short- and long-context budgets

blocks.text: Five model scales and over 100 budget configurations support an additive power law. Constant-Last4 averages the latest four constant-LR checkpoints. A 1.22B trajectory at about 100B LCCP tokens shows no clear saturation within that range, rather than indefinitely. [6]

articles.paper: Harness Scaling for Generalizable Agentic Reinforcement Learning
articles.authors: Fei Bai · Huatong Song · Chuan Hao · Ran Tao · Jian Yang · Bryan Dai · Wayne Xin Zhao · Ji-Rong Wen
articles.title: Harness diversity as another RL scaling axis

blocks.text: A factorized configuration space and balanced factorial coverage create a compact cross-harness curriculum. The authors report transfer to unseen white-box configurations and external black-box harnesses; the abstract does not establish a universal power-law exponent. [7]

articles.paper: Scaling Multilingual Pretraining of Pixel Language Models
articles.authors: Ilker Kesen · Jenny Kunz · Kasra Malihi · Desmond Elliott
articles.title: Pixel LMs: languages, scripts, and capacity scale differently

blocks.text: At fixed per-language compute, three axes are evaluated on five tasks and 83 languages. Capacity mitigates multilingual interference; language/script expansion helps locally, while unseen-script transfer does not keep improving with scale. [8]

articles.paper: Scaling in Games: Continued Pre-Training For Embodied Agents In Diverse Virtual Worlds
articles.authors: Kuan Zhang · Yukun Chen · Zhihao Yang · Yue Su · Xiangnan Wu · Zirong Chen · Run Luo · Jinkun Hou · Tao Tan · Yinhe Zheng · Yiming Li
articles.title: Virtual-world CPT: diversity has limits for distant transfer
articles.dateNote: First October 20 07:09 EDT · v1; overlap-window addition

blocks.text: 120 configurations span 0.8B–27B, 50–1,600 hours, and five mixtures. Diversity helps related-world transfer but has limited distant-world gains; larger single-world models can transfer worse. The authors distinguish early interface learning from later world-specific learning. [9]

articles.paper: Effects of Model Scale and Quantization on Social Bias and Abstention in Question Answering
articles.authors: Kuniko Paxton · Ifeoluwa Wuraola · Dhavalkumar Thakker
articles.title: Fewer biased answers may mean more Unknown responses

blocks.text: On BBQ, larger Qwen3/Gemma-3/SmolLM2 models improve accuracy without a simple bias-scaling trend. Of 26 configurations with fewer biased responses, 20 also increase over-abstention, making refusal and forced-choice controls essential. [10]

articles.paper: Where Should a Stuck Agent Spend Its Next Tokens? Causal Attribution of Inference-Time Resources
articles.authors: Saiyue Lyu · Jerrold Huang · Yunbei Zhang · Janet Wang · Zhenting Wang · Yingqiang Ge · Haibo Zhang
articles.title: After failure: more compute, information, or feedback?
articles.dateNote: First October 20 14:59 EDT · v1; overlap-window addition

blocks.text: BRA fixes the failed state and revision protocol: six models, 194 function-level and 126 repository-level failures. Specifications help consistently; compute's value declines with capability. Three of four frontier models overwhelmingly choose feedback yet gain less than random resource selection. [11]

articles.paper: Mitigating Model Collapse through Dreaming Learning
articles.authors: Matteo Benati · Alessandro Londei · Denise Lanzieri · Raffaello Mastromarino · Vittorio Loreto
articles.title: Low-temperature synthetic-data sharpening and high-temperature dreaming

blocks.text: In a controlled Markov model, recursive Tₛ<1 sampling moves subdominant eigenvalues toward the unit circle, even with data accumulation. A T_d>1 self-sampling regularizer mitigates drift over 5,000 generations and in LSTM/GPT-2 124M tests, without a general LLM guarantee. [12]

articles.paper: Measure First, Then Allocate: Calibrated Rollout Budgets for MCP Agents in Reinforcement Learning
articles.authors: Hieu Tran · Zonghai Yao · Sunjae Kwon · Hong Yu
articles.title: BRACE forecasts within-group reward contrast before generation
articles.dateNote: First October 20 14:15 EDT · v1; overlap-window addition

blocks.text: Historical evidence, success-rate uncertainty, and correlated rewards predict mixed-reward groups before allocation. At three Qwen3-VL scales, fewer new rollouts exceed baseline peaks. Historical-bank collection is accounted for separately, so this is not the same reduction in total training cost. [13]

articles.paper: MemoryTax: The Bitter Lesson of Agent Memory
articles.title: MemoryTax: a stronger reader cannot recover what a writer discarded
articles.evidence: Based on abstract; small empirical study

blocks.text: One LoCoMo conversation, 152 questions, one run per cell compare memory methods across three model capabilities. Writer quality limits designed memory. Photo-caption access explains part of the agent advantage; on 88 photo-free questions, Pi and full context differ by one answer. [14]

articles.paper: Reducing Reward Hacking by Localizing Bad Behavior Instead of Penalizing It
articles.authors: Shawn Hu · Jake Ward · Aria Wong · Nathan Hu · Bryce Woodworth · Alexander Matt Turner · Alex Cloud
articles.title: GRAFT routes gradients with monitor flags, then removes FORGET
articles.evidence: Read full technical blog; not every experiment in the linked paper

blocks.text: Flagged trajectories update only FORGET; unflagged ones update both adapters, with RETAIN-only anchor training. Removing FORGET gives near-zero hacking and nearly +20pp correctness over base in Qwen3-8B/Countdown-Code. RL uses handcrafted monitors and single turns; constructing anchors remains a limitation. [15]

articles.authors: Ben Burtenshaw · Sergio Paniego · Merve Noyan
articles.title: An agent-training roadmap: supervision granularity and rollout bottlenecks

blocks.text: The synthesis connects SFT, distillation, single-turn RL, stateful environments, and full harnesses. Supervision shifts from token probabilities to trajectory outcomes, while long-episode generation becomes the bottleneck. It links corresponding TRL/OpenEnv/AsyncGRPO implementations. [16]

articles.title: ALTK-Evolve distills training-task outcomes into guidelines

blocks.text: GPT-4.1 extracts rules from training trajectories, then freezes them for held-out prompts without weight updates. Retail Pass^4 is 67.5%—all four trials succeed, not pass@4. The leaderboard snapshot is October 12, and longer guidelines increase token use. [17]

classic.paper: Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models
classic.authors: Jared Kaplan · Sam McCandlish · Tom Henighan · Tom B. Brown · Benjamin Chess · Rewon Child · Scott Gray · Alec Radford · Jeffrey Wu · Dario Amodei
classic.title: Kaplan scaling laws: identify the resource that limits loss
classic.dateNote: First 2020-01-22 22:59 EST (January 23 UTC); read v1; year refers to the technical report
classic.evidence: Read §1.2 and §§4–6 with fitting setup; empirical laws, not universal theorems

recognition.label: Foundational scaling-laws work; OpenAlex record: 1,745 citations (checked 2026-10-22)

classic.question: If data and LR schedules become optimization variables, how much of the fitted C-to-N exponent is a property of the training protocol?

blocks.text: After Transformers (2017) and GPT-2 (2019), the allocation question was larger models versus longer training. This work relates WebText2 token cross-entropy to non-embedding parameters N, data D, steps S, and tokens per step B. [18]

blocks.label: Each empirical fit requires the other resources not to bind; the three laws cannot simply be multiplied
The joint fit recovers a single-resource law when one term dominates
Learning curves are fitted after warmup; Sₘᵢₙ adjusts for batch size

blocks.tex: B_{\rm crit}(L)\simeq B_*L^{-1/\alpha_B},\quad\alpha_B\simeq0.21,\qquad S_{\min}=\frac{S}{1+B_{\rm crit}/B},\qquad C_{\min}=\frac{6NBS}{1+B/B_{\rm crit}}
blocks.label: Actual FLOPs differ from adjusted minimum compute; the model includes parallelism efficiency

blocks.tex: \alpha_C=\left(\alpha_N^{-1}+\alpha_B^{-1}+\alpha_S^{-1}\right)^{-1},\qquad N\propto C_{\min}^{\alpha_C/\alpha_N},\quad B\propto C_{\min}^{\alpha_C/\alpha_B},\quad S_{\min}\propto C_{\min}^{\alpha_C/\alpha_S}
blocks.label: Allocation exponents follow from the fitted training model, rather than guessing from three one-dimensional curves

blocks.caption: Section 6: predicted and empirical exponents differ; empirical D=BS grows roughly as Cₘᵢₙ^0.27. [18]

blocks.title: Evidence boundary
blocks.text: The exponents depend on data, tokenizer, optimizer, and budget adjustments; §6.3 identifies extrapolation contradictions. Chinchilla, read October 17, later revised allocation under a different protocol. [18]
